svg.title: A ripple-carry and a Kogge-Stone adder for 8 bits, every gate and wire, verified on all inputs
svg.text: the same sums in 7 logic levels instead of 15, for 1.8 times the gates
Both networks are built, checked and laid out by figure.py.
Every gate and wire is drawn. A wire is darker the more often it carries a 1 over all 65,536 pairs of inputs; depth, the longest path, is what limits the speed.
Checked before drawing: each network gives a + b on all 65,536 pairs. ripple carry passes the
carry from bit to bit, so its last sum waits 15 levels; Kogge-Stone works the carries out side by
side in 7, with 1.8 times the gates. The darkest wire is 1 in 50 % of the cases.
